# HQ documentation

> Documentation for HQ, the company brain your AI runs on: guides, product references, architecture, security, and development docs for HQ Core, the HQ CLI, HQ Cloud and sync, the console, fleet agents, deploy, the hq-pro platform, packages, secrets, sharing and HQ MCP.

Last updated: 2026-10-20

Product overview, pricing and use cases live on the product site: https://hqforwork.com/llms.txt

## Product Guide

- [What is HQ?](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/guide/1-what-is-hq/): HQ is infrastructure for orchestrating AI workers, autonomous agents that code, write, research, and automate
- [Getting Started](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/guide/2-getting-started/): Install the HQ desktop app and open your workspace in Claude Code or Codex
- [Core Concepts](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/guide/3-core-concepts/): The mental model behind HQ, workers, knowledge, commands, checkpoints, and the INDEX.md system
- [Commands](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/guide/4-commands/): Reference for HQ slash commands
- [Workers](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/guide/5-workers/): Reference for reusable HQ worker definitions, including development, content, and standalone workers
- [Knowledge Bases](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/guide/6-knowledge-bases/): Persistent memory for your AI workers, built-in bases, company knowledge, and the symlink-to-git pattern
- [Projects](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/guide/7-projects/): Project management in HQ, PRDs, the Ralph loop, and autonomous execution
- [Cloud Sync](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/guide/8-cloud-sync/): Sync your HQ to the cloud for mobile access via the PWA dashboard
- [Work Mesh](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/guide/9-work-mesh/): Automatic presence and session activity via hq mesh daemon, context, and session verbs
- [Use HQ free, self-hosted or on-prem](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/guide/use-hq-for-free/): Run HQ core and the HQ CLI on your own computers or servers with no HQ account and no HQ cloud. For advanced, enterprise and government teams that need to keep their work on their own machines

## Products

- [hq-core](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-core/): The HQ scaffold and starter kit, the create-hq seed that bootstraps a new HQ instance
- [hq-cli](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-cli/): The hq CLI, module management and cloud sync, the operator's entry point to the HQ ecosystem
- [HQ anywhere](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-anywhere/): Install HQ for Claude Code and Codex, connect hosted MCP clients, and check or remove your setup
- [hq-cloud](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-cloud/): The HQ cloud sync engine, bidirectional S3 sync that backs the hq CLI and the hq-sync menubar app
- [HQ desktop app](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-sync/): One desktop app that installs HQ, opens your workspace in an AI tool, and keeps it synced
- [HQ Workspace](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-workspace/): HQ Workspace, the agent-first email and calendar substrate for HQ. Cloud webmail, an agent API, and a native MCP endpoint your agents query directly
- [hq-console](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-console/): The HQ Console is a Next.js 15 admin UI for HQ deployments, teams, and usage, authenticated over the shared Cognito identity
- [Grok Build Desktop](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/grok-build-desktop/): A native macOS workspace for running Grok Build, Codex, and Claude Code in durable parallel sessions
- [Fleet Agents](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/fleet-agents/): Persistent AI teammates with managed runtimes, company access, and their own communication channels
- [Create an agent](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/fleet-agents/create/): Choose a Fleet Agent size, review its monthly cost, provision the runtime, and complete authentication
- [Configure an agent](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/fleet-agents/configuration/): Reference for Fleet Agent identity, model, reasoning, speed, membership, ownership, groups, and controls
- [Connect channels](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/fleet-agents/channels/): Connect Fleet Agents to Slack, email, and Telegram, then control who can call them
- [Access and security](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/fleet-agents/access/): Control Fleet Agent roles, ownership, groups, vault access, callers, and deprovisioning
- [Operate and troubleshoot](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/fleet-agents/operations/): Monitor Fleet Agent health, control its lifecycle, use the CLI, and resolve common setup or channel failures
- [Agent sizes and billing](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/fleet-agents/sizes-and-billing/): The four Fleet Agent box sizes and their prices, legacy prices for existing customers, and how size changes are approved and billed
- [HQ Deploy Platform](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-deploy/introduction/): A complete PaaS for deploying static and SSR web applications to AWS
- [Authentication](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-deploy/authentication/): Dual auth system, Clerk JWT and API keys
- [CloudFormation Template](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-deploy/cfn-template/): Parameterized IaC template for provisioning customer data plane resources
- [Deploy CLI](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-deploy/cli/): The hq-deploy CLI, framework detection, API key login, and one-command deploys
- [In-Context Comments](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-deploy/comments/): Viewers leave feedback directly on a gated deploy, anchored to a point or a region, tagged to their identity, behind the same access gate as the deploy
- [Custom Deploy Domains (Enterprise)](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-deploy/custom-domains/): Serve every deploy under your own domain, {app}.your-domain.com, with automated wildcard certificates and DNS validation
- [DNS & Domains](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-deploy/dns-domains/): App registration, subdomain generation, and Route 53 DNS management
- [E2E Tests](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-deploy/e2e-tests/): End-to-end test infrastructure for validating deploys against real AWS staging
- [Enterprise Init](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-deploy/enterprise-init/): Provision HQ Deploy infrastructure in a customer's AWS account via CloudFormation
- [Multi-Tenant Orgs](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-deploy/multi-tenant/): Organization model with resource isolation across tenants
- [SSR Deploys](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-deploy/ssr-flow/): Server-rendered app deployment via ECS Fargate, ECR, and ALB
- [Static Deploys](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-deploy/static-flow/): How static sites are deployed via S3, CloudFront, and Lambda@Edge
- [Upgrades](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-deploy/upgrades/): Enterprise stack upgrade flow with ChangeSet preview and dry-run support
- [HQ Pro, Vault, Teams & Identity](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-pro/about/): The HQ Pro backend, encrypted vault with capability-based access, the team platform, shared Cognito identity, and onboarding
- [Setup channel lifecycle](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-pro/setup-channel-lifecycle/): Create a company, turn on cloud, set up billing, and create the first agent inside the desktop app, with no console or CLI required
- [Pricing API](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-pro/pricing-api/): The public GET /v1/pricing endpoint that states the HQ usage card, box sizes, signup options, legacy plans and billing rules
- [Billing and usage](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-pro/billing-and-usage/): The HQ usage card, the vault fee, the 30-day trial and its $500 cap, the $10 of usage included each month, the spend limit, boxes and deploy extras
- [Requesting Access](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-pro/access/): How new users get into HQ Cloud and HQ Pro, the demo-gated access flow
- [Team Commands (v0)](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-pro/commands-v0/): In-HQ slash commands for team invites and bidirectional sync
- [GitHub Auth](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-pro/github-auth/): GitHub OAuth replacing Cognito, device flow, self-signed JWTs, DynamoDB storage
- [Team Onboarding](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-pro/onboarding/): CLI-native team onboarding, admin creation and member invite acceptance
- [HQ Installer](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-pro/overview/): Native macOS installer that replaces the CLI onboarding with a signed, notarized .dmg wizard
- [Team Platform](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-pro/platform/): Multi-tenant team management with entitlement packs and content sharing
- [Quickstart](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-pro/quickstart/): Download the HQ Installer and walk through the 11-screen wizard
- [Troubleshooting](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-pro/troubleshooting/): Common failure modes in the HQ Installer and how to resolve them
- [Package System](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-packages/overview/): Modular package ecosystem for extending HQ with workers, commands, knowledge, and policies
- [Claude Merge](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-packages/claude-merge/): How Claude Code merges package contents into HQ directories with conflict detection
- [CLI Install Flow](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-packages/cli-install/): How packages are downloaded, verified, and extracted via the hq-cli
- [Registry API](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-packages/registry-api/): Package discovery, download, and admin management API hosted in indigo-nx
- [Package Spec v2](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/hq-packages/spec-v2/): Security-first package specification with RSA signing and content allow-lists

## Capabilities

- [External Connections](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/capabilities/external-connections/): Issue scoped, read-only credentials that let external agents and services read selected prefixes of your company vault, no SSO required, revocable in one click, every read audited
- [hq-share](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/capabilities/hq-share/): Mint single-use share-session links for HQ vault paths, a browser ACL picker that grants multiple recipients per-recipient read/write in one batch
- [hq-secrets](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/capabilities/hq-secrets/): Schema-driven secret access for HQ, inject secrets into commands without ever printing them, with company/personal scoping and per-secret ACLs
- [Slack Bot Factory](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/capabilities/slack-bot-factory/): The fastest way to get HQ into a Slack workspace, connect a workspace once, then mint per-bot Slack apps on demand. Multi-tenant, vault-backed, and idempotent on re-auth
- [Message forwarding](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/products/capabilities/message-forwarding/): Forward an HQ direct message or channel message, with its Details or Prompt card, to a person, bot, or channel from the desktop app or the hq CLI. Forwards to people and bots can include files
- [HQ MCP](https://docs.hq.computer/hq-in-chat/): Use Indigo HQ from ChatGPT, Claude.ai, and connected agents through the cloud connector

## Architecture

- [Architecture Overview](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/architecture/1-overview/): System architecture of the HQ ecosystem, the split repos, data flow, infrastructure, and technology choices
- [Ecosystem & Repo Map](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/architecture/2-ecosystem/): How the HQ ecosystem is split across independently versioned repos, what each repo is, how they compose, and where they ship
- [create-hq](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/architecture/3-create-hq/): Architecture of the create-hq installer, the npx create-hq scaffolding tool that bootstraps a new HQ instance
- [hq-cli](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/architecture/4-hq-cli/): Architecture of the @indigoai-us/hq-cli package, module management, sync strategies, and cloud sync bridge
- [hq-cloud](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/architecture/5-hq-cloud/): Deep dive into @indigoai-us/hq-cloud, the S3 sync engine that powers bidirectional file synchronization between a local HQ instance and IndigoAI cloud storage
- [Infrastructure](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/architecture/6-infrastructure/): AWS infrastructure defined with SST, Cognito auth, S3 storage, API Gateway, and CloudFront distribution
- [PWA Dashboard](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/architecture/7-pwa/): Architecture of the HQ web app, React 19, Vite, Cognito auth, file API, and PWA installability
- [Module System](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/architecture/8-module-system/): How HQ manages knowledge bases, workers, and shared content through a declarative module manifest with multiple sync strategies
- [API Reference](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/architecture/9-api-reference/): REST API endpoints for the HQ Cloud API, covering file operations, authentication, and S3 storage

## Security

- [Security & Trust](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/security/1-overview/): How HQ protects customer data, tenant isolation, encryption, identity and access, AI model-provider handling, subprocessors, and current limitations
- [Subprocessors](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/security/2-subprocessors/): The third parties Indigo engages to process customer data when providing HQ, what they do, the data involved, and where they process it
- [Tenant Isolation](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/security/3-tenant-isolation/): How HQ guarantees that one organization can never read or write another organization's data, through physical, cryptographic, and credential-scoped separation
- [Data Security & Encryption](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/security/4-data-security-encryption/): How HQ classifies, encrypts, controls, retains, and deletes customer data, at rest, in transit, in secrets stores, and through capability-based sharing
- [Identity & Access Management](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/security/5-identity-access-management/): How users and machines authenticate to HQ, how requests are authorized, and how Indigo controls its own administrative access
- [Infrastructure & Network Security](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/security/6-infrastructure-network-security/): The cloud infrastructure HQ runs on, how it is provisioned, isolated, monitored, and operated on managed AWS services
- [Application Security & SDLC](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/security/7-application-security-sdlc/): How HQ is built, tested, and shipped, and the controls that keep security defects out of production
- [Shared Responsibility](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/security/8-shared-responsibility/): The division of security duties between AWS, Indigo, and the customer, and why HQ's local-agent model puts some controls on the customer side by design
- [Business Continuity & Incident Response](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/security/9-business-continuity-incident-response/): How HQ stays available, recovers from failures, and responds to security incidents, stated with both what is in place today and what is being formalized
- [Compliance Roadmap](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/security/10-compliance-roadmap/): Indigo's compliance posture for HQ, stated honestly, what we align to today, what we are actively building, and what is planned
- [Vulnerability Disclosure](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/security/11-vulnerability-disclosure/): How to report a potential vulnerability in HQ, what is in scope, the safe-harbor terms, and what to expect from Indigo
- [CAIQ Questionnaire](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/security/12-caiq-questionnaire/): A pre-filled, CAIQ-style security questionnaire organized by Cloud Controls Matrix domains, to collapse the back-and-forth of a vendor security review

## Development

- [Local Setup](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/development/1-local-setup/): Clone and run the individual HQ ecosystem repos locally for development and testing
- [Deploying Infrastructure](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/development/2-deploying-infra/): Deploy HQ's AWS infrastructure using SST for serverless backend, auth, storage, and CDN
- [Publishing Packages](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/development/3-publishing-packages/): Per-repo npm + release workflow for the HQ ecosystem packages
- [Template Updates](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/development/4-template-updates/): Managing the HQ template content that ships with create-hq
- [Testing](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/development/5-testing/): Testing strategy and QA processes across the HQ ecosystem repos
- [Contributing](https://docs.hq.computer/hq/development/6-contributing/): Contribution guidelines for the HQ ecosystem repos, how to fork, branch, commit, and submit pull requests

## Reference

- [Glossary](https://docs.hq.computer/glossary/): Plain definitions for the vocabulary of agent-native teams, Agent Amnesia, shared context layer, team AI operating system, MCP, workers, skills, policies, and data gravity
- [HQ vs. the alternatives](https://docs.hq.computer/comparison/): How HQ compares to static context files (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md), Cursor & Windsurf rules, raw MCP servers, and agent-memory tools, and where a synced, team-wide context layer fits
